gen-dafont-early-gameboy-mulish: Chunky pixel swagger, loosely spaced. Mulish takes over below with a ruler-straight line weight and a tall lowercase, so paragraphs flow along smoothly and never feel crowded.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-roboto-slab: Playful, spaced-out arcade lettering up top. Roboto Slab holds the lines below with sturdy structure and open throats, and that firm, orderly footing is the strongest thing about the pairing.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-bitter: Classic in spirit, Edo SZ stands its lowercase tall like cast iron capitals with one constant stroke width. And Bitter, a slab-serif with a huge lowercase eye and see-through s shapes, keeps running paragraphs grounded and dependable.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-glegoo: Cast-iron stature in lowercase form, drawn with a single fixed stroke. Edo SZ is best at that monumental, cultural display, but Glegoo is best at refined text, with big counters and wide unclosed mouths.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-inter: Edo SZ stands its lowercase tall as cast iron capitals. Inter, a sans with hollow-reed counters and a smooth tube-like line, sits beneath it, quietly letting that sturdy heading take the spotlight.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-kadwa: Towering lowercase, adventurous and widely spaced. Kadwa, a text serif, does the quieter work of open-ended curves and a generous x-height, while Eight Bit Dragon owns the bold, lighter-horizontal display moment.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-suwannaph: Suwannaphum brings dignified serif letters, with a wide-open c and a high x-height. Eight Bit Dragon, by contrast, excels at bold, widely spaced display, with thick-thin variation that never thins to hairlines.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-pridi: Electroharmonix breaks every word into single, commanding letters. Pridi, a classic serif with generous curve openings and almost capital-sized small letters, supplies the refined, strongest counterweight to all that striking display.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-inter: Electroharmonix splits each word into striking single letters with open-handed curves. Inter follows with a plain sans smoothness, like drawn wire, so sentences glide along without ever tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-rubik: Gaps that split each word into single letters give Electroharmonix its commanding look. And Rubik, a plain sans with big lowercase and soft, open rounds, keeps paragraphs clear and friendly even at small sizes.
